stress_overwhelm.description: Measures acute mental pressure, physical tension, and repetitive overthinking.

emotional_wellbeing.description: Evaluates baseline daily happiness, emotional regulation under setbacks, and future optimism.

sleep_vitality.description: Assesses restorative sleep quality, physical energy stamina, and daytime concentration.

questions.text: 1. How likely are you to wake up feeling well-rested, energized, and refreshed for the day?
2. How likely are you to take dedicated personal time for yourself each day to unwind and relax?
3. How likely are you to feel genuinely happy, content, and positive in your day-to-day routine?
4. How likely are you to feel overwhelmed or weighed down by your daily academic or personal responsibilities?
5. How likely are you to experience physical tension, nervousness, or racing thoughts under pressure?
6. When unexpected challenges or setbacks occur, how likely are you to stay calm and emotionally balanced?
7. How likely are you to maintain mental clarity, concentration, and motivation throughout your daily tasks?
8. When facing difficult stress, how likely are you to actively use healthy coping habits (e.g. exercise, walks, hobbies, mindfulness)?
9. How likely are you to reach out to friends, family, or mentors when you need emotional comfort or guidance?
10. How likely do you feel valued, respected, and socially connected within your peer community?
11. How likely are you to get trapped in repetitive overthinking, self-doubt, or worry about future outcomes?
12. How likely are you to feel hopeful, motivated, and optimistic about your future and personal growth?

personas.title: The Thriving Anchor
personas.tagline: High Emotional Balance, Quality Rest & Healthy Boundaries
personas.summary: You demonstrate high emotional stability, solid restorative sleep, and proactive self-care. You protect your personal boundaries well and navigate academic/life pressures with steady composure.

personas.title: The High-Drive Overextender
personas.tagline: Strong Dedication with Slumping Self-Care & Sleep Deficit
personas.summary: You are giving 100% of your energy to responsibilities, but your own personal reserves are running dangerously low. Disrupted sleep and lack of dedicated 'me-time' are causing cognitive friction.

personas.title: The Overthinking Navigator
personas.summary: You are experiencing acute mental tension and repetitive loop worrying. Demands feel magnified right now, making nervous system de-escalation and structured task triage your top priorities.

personas.title: The Isolated Explorer
personas.tagline: Low Social Reach-Out with Independent Struggles
personas.summary: You tend to carry emotional weight quietly on your own. Reconnecting with trusted peers or mentors will dramatically lighten your cognitive load and rebuild feelings of community belonging.

personas.title: The Steady Harmonizer
personas.tagline: Manageable Baselines with Opportunities for Enhancement
personas.summary: You are navigating daily life with moderate stability. While your emotional and stress baselines are manageable, incorporating intentional sleep rituals and self-care pauses will unlock greater focus and happiness.

stress_overwhelm.detail: Perform two sharp inhales through the nose followed by a slow 6-second exhale through the mouth for 3 minutes to instantly drop sympathetic cortisol arousal.
Write all looming concerns on paper each evening. Group them into 'Within My Control' vs 'Beyond My Control' to halt nighttime thought loops.
Establish a hard stop on study/work materials at least 45 minutes before sleep to prevent nervous system stimulation.

self_care.detail: Schedule 20 minutes solely for yourself today ? no notifications, no work, just listening to music, sketching, or enjoying a warm beverage.
Replace doom-scrolling breaks with physical movement ? a brisk 15-minute outdoor walk or gentle stretching between study blocks.
Schedule personal hobbies on your calendar with the same priority as academic deadlines, treating self-care as essential fuel.

sleep_vitality.detail: Step outside for 10-15 minutes of natural morning sunlight within 30 minutes of waking to anchor your circadian rhythm and natural alertness.
Maintain a consistent wake-up time within a 45-minute window every day, even on weekends, to stabilize REM and deep restorative sleep.
Keep your sleeping room cool (19?C / 66?F), dark, and free from bright blue LEDs to stimulate natural melatonin production.

emotional_wellbeing.detail: Identify three specific moments today that brought comfort or a smile, actively savoring the positive feeling for 20 seconds.
Notice moments of harsh self-criticism and consciously reframe the dialogue into compassionate, constructive coaching.
Spend at least 2 hours every weekend pursuing a creative or recreational activity purely for intrinsic joy rather than external praise.

social_connection.detail: Send a simple message or voice note to one friend or family member sharing a warm thought or funny memory.
Work or study alongside peers in communal spaces (library, campus lounge, caf?) to experience social presence without social fatigue.
Nurture regular conversations with a trusted mentor or peer where you can speak honestly about ongoing feelings and mutual goals.
